ES-IS.why: OSI End System to Intermediate System routing protocol (ISO 9542), a documented historic protocol. evidence: memory (no source)

BACnet.why: Building-automation protocol published as ASHRAE 135 / ISO 16484-5. Specialist tier fits. evidence: memory (no source)

AMQP.why: OASIS-standardised messaging protocol, widely used. Race condition is a reasonable tier for specialists. evidence: memory (no source)

HTTP/3.why: Specified in RFC 9114. Developers know it, so a null-pointer tier fits. Aliases HTTP3 and HTTP version 3 are phrasings of the same name. evidence: memory (no source)

High-Speed SECS Message Service.why: SEMI E37 standard for semiconductor equipment communication. HSMS is an abbreviation alias. evidence: memory (no source)

POP3.why: RFC 1939, known by nearly everyone, so off-by-one fits. Alias 'POP' is a common English word and is too generic; it should be dropped. evidence: memory (no source)

Telnet.why: RFC 854, well known, so off-by-one fits. Alias 'telnet protocol' is a case and generic-noun variant, which is fine. evidence: memory (no source)

Daytime.why: RFC 867 daytime protocol (port 13). Obscure but a named, specified protocol, so memory-leak tier for systems people fits. evidence: memory (no source)

gRPC.why: Google's RPC framework with a documented protocol spec on grpc.io. Null-pointer tier fits. Alias 'Google RPC' is doubtful: it is not a clear plain binding of gRPC and could mean Google's internal RPC. evidence: memory (no source)

FTAM.why: OSI File Transfer, Access and Management, ISO 8571. Documented historic protocol, so race tier fits. evidence: memory (no source)

TCP.why: RFC 793, universally known, so off-by-one fits. Alias 'Transmission Control Protocol' is the expansion. evidence: memory (no source)

IEEE 802.15.4.why: IEEE standard for low-rate wireless PANs. Alias 802.15.4 is the short form. Specialist tier fits. evidence: memory (no source)

EIGRP.why: Cisco routing protocol, documented in vendor docs and RFC 7868. Networking specialists know it, so race tier fits. evidence: memory (no source)

AFP.why: Apple Filing Protocol, documented by Apple as a vendor protocol. Alias is the expansion. Specialist tier fits. evidence: memory (no source)

Diameter.why: RFC 6733, the AAA protocol. Telecom specialists know it, so race tier fits. evidence: memory (no source)

9P.why: Plan 9 file protocol, documented in Plan 9 manuals. Specialist tier fits. evidence: memory (no source)

AYIYA.why: Anything In Anything IPv6 tunnelling protocol with a published spec and implementations. Very obscure, so heisenbug tier fits. evidence: memory (no source)

GIOP.why: OMG CORBA General Inter-ORB Protocol. Alias is the expansion. Specialist tier fits. evidence: memory (no source)

EtherNet/IP.why: ODVA industrial protocol. ENIP is the standard abbreviation. Specialist tier fits. evidence: memory (no source)

eDonkey.why: Documented (reverse-engineered) historic P2P protocol, the eDonkey2000 network. Memory-leak tier for domain people fits. evidence: memory (no source)
